answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Work waits on the ledge until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the reef of the next round. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, revoked by a single upheld challenge, idle agents bleed standing. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the signal of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
